## Ethics Statement

This work studies coding agents that predict the downstream consequences of
software changes. Our experiments use procedurally generated systems and
permissively licensed open-source software; they involve no human subjects,
personal data, or user-generated content. The proposed techniques may help
identify cross-component failures before software changes are deployed, but
similar capabilities could also reveal structural weaknesses in software
systems. Our experiments are restricted to systems and environments under the
experimenter’s control. We encourage deployment only with appropriate
authorization, access controls, and human oversight for consequential software
changes.

## Reproducibility Statement

Training and evaluation
worlds are disjoint, corpus generation is seeded, and each reported training
condition retains its data split, configuration, random seeds, and model
checkpoint. Executed transitions—rather than model-generated judgments—serve
as supervision for downstream consequences. For the main agent experiments, we
retain per-task outputs and report results across training seeds with
world-clustered uncertainty estimates. The appendices document the software
worlds and graph schema, exploration and evaluation protocols, model training
details, decision accounting, and complete experimental results.
